text: El tiempo es cerebro: cómo reconocer los síntomas de un derrame cerebral con el método F.A.S.T. Admin marzo 31, 2026 Heart and Stroke Tabla de Contenido En un caso de ictus, cada segundo cuenta. Quizás hayas oído la frase «El tiempo es cerebro». No es solo un dicho médico; es una realidad clínica.Según los NIH (Institutos Nacionales de la Salud de EE. UU.), durante un ictus, el cerebro se ve privado de oxígeno y mueren aproximadamente 1,9 millones de neuronas por cada minuto que se interrumpe el flujo sanguíneo.Si se encuentra en el área metropolitana de Dallas-Fort Worth, saber reconocer los síntomas y dónde encontrar atención de emergencia para un derrame cerebral en Dallas puede marcar la diferencia entre una recuperación completa y una discapacidad permanente.Esta guía está diseñada para ayudarle a comprender qué es un derrame cerebral, cómo reconocerlo de inmediato y por qué actuar con prontitud es fundamental. Para el panorama completo de emergencias cardiovasculares cerca de White Rock, incluidos ataque al corazón y coágulos de sangre, vea nuestra guía pilar.¿Qué ocurre durante un ictus? (Isquémico vs. Hemorrágico)Un derrame cerebral es esencialmente un «ataque cerebral». Ocurre cuando algo bloquea el suministro de sangre a una parte del cerebro o cuando se rompe un vaso sanguíneo en el cerebro. Según los Centros para el Control y la Prevención de Enfermedades (CDC) , existen dos tipos principales de accidentes cerebrovasculares:Accidente cerebrovascular isquémico: Este es el tipo más común, representando aproximadamente el 87% de todos los casos. Ocurre cuando el flujo sanguíneo a través de la arteria que suministra sangre rica en oxígeno al cerebro se bloquea, a menudo por un coágulo de sangre.Accidente cerebrovascular hemorrágico: ocurre cuando una arteria del cerebro pierde sangre o se rompe. La sangre derramada ejerce demasiada presión sobre las células cerebrales, dañándolas. La hipertensión arterial y los aneurismas son causas comunes.Independientemente del tipo, el resultado es el mismo: las células cerebrales comienzan a morir porque no pueden obtener el oxígeno y los nutrientes que necesitan para funcionar.La «hora dorada» del tratamiento del ictus.En el ámbito de la medicina de urgencias, hablamos de la «hora dorada». Esta se refiere a los primeros 60 minutos tras la aparición de los síntomas de un ictus.Si bien la intervención médica es eficaz después de esta hora, los Institutos Nacionales de la Salud (NIH) recalcan que cuanto antes comience el tratamiento, mayor será la probabilidad de preservar la función cerebral y reducir las complicaciones a largo plazo.Buscar atención de emergencia para un accidente cerebrovascular en Dallas dentro de este plazo permite a los médicos utilizar técnicas avanzadas de imagen y medicamentos que salvan vidas, cuyo uso es extremadamente urgente.El método FAST para identificar un accidente cerebrovascularReconocer un derrame cerebral no requiere un título médico. Según los CDC , el acrónimo FAST es una forma sencilla de recordar los síntomas repentinos de un derrame cerebral.Cara caídaPídele a la persona que sonría. ¿Se le cae un lado de la cara o se le entumece? Una sonrisa asimétrica es una señal de alarma importante.Debilidad en el brazoPídele a la persona que levante ambos brazos. ¿Se le cae uno de ellos? La debilidad o el entumecimiento, especialmente en un solo lado del cuerpo, es un síntoma clásico.Dificultad para hablarPídele a la persona que repita una frase sencilla, como «El cielo es azul». ¿Su habla es confusa? ¿No puede hablar o es difícil de entender?Es hora de llamar al 911.Si la persona presenta alguno de estos síntomas, incluso si desaparecen, llame al 911 de inmediato. Anote la hora en que aparecieron los primeros síntomas. Esta información es vital para el equipo que brinda atención de emergencia por accidentes cerebrovasculares en Dallas .Síntomas atípicos de un accidente cerebrovascular que usted debe conocerSi bien la ecografía FAST abarca los signos más comunes, los accidentes cerebrovasculares a veces pueden presentarse de manera menos evidente, particularmente en mujeres o en pacientes de edad avanzada.Mareos repentinos, pérdida del equilibrio y cambios en la visión.Los CDC señalan que la dificultad repentina para caminar, el mareo, la pérdida del equilibrio o la coordinación pueden indicar un accidente cerebrovascular que afecta al cerebelo. Además, la visión borrosa repentina o la pérdida de visión en uno o ambos ojos nunca deben ignorarse.Señales de alerta de un AIT (miniictus)Un ataque isquémico transitorio (AIT) se conoce comúnmente como «mini-ictus». Según los Institutos Nacionales de la Salud (NIH) , se produce por una interrupción temporal del flujo sanguíneo al cerebro.Si bien los síntomas pueden durar solo unos minutos y luego desaparecer, un AIT es una señal de alerta importante que indica que un ictus completo podría ser inminente. Un AIT debe tratarse como una emergencia médica.Por qué debes ir a urgencias inmediatamenteQuizás sienta la tentación de esperar a ver si los síntomas mejoran, o incluso de intentar conducir usted mismo a una clínica. Por favor, no lo haga. Llamar al 911 es fundamental, ya que los paramédicos pueden iniciar los protocolos de reanimación en cuanto lleguen.También pueden alertar al equipo de atención de accidentes cerebrovasculares del hospital para que se active el protocolo de emergencia antes incluso de que usted entre por la puerta.El estrecho margen de tiempo para los fármacos trombolíticos (tPA)Para los accidentes cerebrovasculares isquémicos, los médicos pueden usar un medicamento llamado activador tisular del plasminógeno (tPA). Este fármaco actúa disolviendo el coágulo de sangre y restableciendo el flujo sanguíneo.Sin embargo, las guías de los NIH ( Institutos Nacionales de la Salud de EE. UU.) indican que, por lo general, el tPA debe administrarse entre 3 y 4,5 horas después del inicio de los síntomas para que sea eficaz y seguro. Si se espera demasiado, esta opción que puede salvar vidas podría no estar disponible.Diagnóstico rápido y atención de emergencia para accidentes cerebrovasculares en DallasDallas alberga algunos de los centros especializados en accidentes cerebrovasculares más importantes del país. Cuando llegue a un servicio de urgencias para recibir atención médica por un accidente cerebrovascular en Dallas , el equipo actuará con una rapidez asombrosa.Los pasos de diagnóstico suelen incluir:Tomografía computarizada o resonancia magnética: para determinar el tipo de accidente cerebrovascular y su ubicación.Ecografía carotídea: para comprobar el flujo sanguíneo en las arterias del cuello.Análisis de sangre: para comprobar la velocidad de coagulación y los niveles de glucosa.Al elegir un centro equipado para la intervención neurológica rápida, usted se asegura de recibir la atención de la más alta calidad en esos primeros minutos críticos.Diagnóstico rápido y atención de emergencia para accidentes cerebrovasculares en DallasDallas alberga algunos de los centros especializados en accidentes cerebrovasculares más importantes del país. Cuando llegue a la sala de emergencias de White Rock para recibir atención médica urgente por un accidente cerebrovascular en Dallas , el equipo actuará con una rapidez increíble.Los pasos de diagnóstico suelen incluir:Tomografía computarizada o resonancia magnética: para determinar el tipo de accidente cerebrovascular y su ubicación.Ecografía carotídea: para comprobar el flujo sanguíneo en las arterias del cuello.Análisis de sangre: para comprobar la velocidad de coagulación y los niveles de glucosa.Al elegir un centro equipado para la intervención neurológica rápida, usted se asegura de recibir la atención de la más alta calidad en esos primeros minutos críticos.Acude ahora mismo a la sala de urgencias de White Rock para obtener un alivio rápido y atención especializada.¿Necesita atención inmediata? Llámenos ahora al (469) 943-2939Manténgase informado con consejos de salud de temporada, recomendaciones de primeros auxilios y maneras prácticas de cuidar su bienestar durante todo el año. Siga a ER of White Rock en Facebook e Instagram para obtener valiosas actualizaciones sobre salud.Preguntas frecuentes¿Puede producirse un ictus a cualquier edad?Sí. Si bien el riesgo aumenta con la edad, los accidentes cerebrovasculares pueden ocurrirle a cualquiera, incluidos niños y adultos jóvenes. Los factores relacionados con el estilo de vida y las afecciones preexistentes influyen significativamente.¿Cuál es la diferencia entre un derrame cerebral y un ataque cardíaco?Un infarto es un problema de circulación en el corazón, mientras que un derrame cerebral es un problema de circulación o hemorragia en el cerebro. Ambas son emergencias potencialmente mortales.¿Debo tomar aspirina si creo que estoy sufriendo un derrame cerebral?No. No tome aspirina a menos que un médico se lo indique. Si está sufriendo un accidente cerebrovascular hemorrágico (con sangrado), la aspirina podría empeorar la hemorragia.¿Por qué es mejor llamar al 911 que conducir hasta la sala de emergencias?Los Servicios Médicos de Emergencia (EMS, por sus siglas en inglés) pueden comenzar el tratamiento de inmediato y están capacitados para evitar los hospitales que no están equipados para tratar accidentes cerebrovasculares, llevándolo directamente a un centro especializado en atención de emergencia para accidentes cerebrovasculares en Dallas .¿Los síntomas de un accidente cerebrovascular son diferentes en las mujeres?En ocasiones, las mujeres pueden presentar síntomas únicos, como hipo repentino, náuseas o debilidad general, además de los signos tradicionales del FAST.Últimas Publicaciones: ¿Cuánto Dura una Visita a la Sala de Emergencias? text: ¿Es un esguince o una fractura? ¿Cuándo acudir a nuestra sala de emergencias en White Rock? Admin marzo 24, 2026 Trauma and Injury Tabla de Contenido Los accidentes no avisan. Ya sea una caída durante una excursión de fin de semana, un resbalón en un suelo mojado o una colisión deportiva, una lesión ortopédica puede ocurrir en un instante. En esos primeros minutos de dolor intenso, la pregunta siempre es la misma: «¿Es solo un esguince o me he roto algo?»Saber diferenciar entre una lesión y otra no solo te dará tranquilidad, sino que también te ayudará a prevenir complicaciones a largo plazo. Si bien algunas lesiones menores pueden tratarse en casa, otras requieren el equipo especializado y la experiencia de un servicio de urgencias.Si buscas tratamiento para una fractura en White Rock, Texas , saber cuándo es conveniente seguir adelante y cuándo acudir a urgencias es el primer paso hacia una recuperación completa. Esta guía cubre la decisión específica entre esguince y fractura; para el panorama más amplio que incluye lesiones de cabeza, conmoción, trauma ocular y dolor de espalda, ve nuestra guía pilar sobre emergencias de huesos, articulaciones y trauma cerca de White Rock.Entendiendo la diferencia: Fracturas óseas vs. Esguinces gravesPara un ojo inexperto, una fractura (el término médico para un hueso roto) y un esguince pueden parecer muy similares. Ambos causan dolor, hinchazón y dificultad para moverse. Sin embargo, afectan a estructuras corporales completamente diferentes.¿Qué ocurre durante un esguince?Un esguince es una lesión en un ligamento, que es el tejido fibroso y resistente que conecta dos huesos en las articulaciones. Cuando una articulación se tuerce o se estira más allá de su rango normal de movimiento, estos ligamentos pueden estirarse demasiado o incluso romperse.Si bien se puede escuchar un chasquido durante un esguince, el hueso en sí permanece intacto.Los diferentes tipos de fracturas óseasLa AAOS afirma que una fractura se produce cuando se aplica al hueso una fuerza mayor de la que este puede soportar. En el ámbito médico, las clasificamos para determinar el mejor tratamiento:Fracturas por estrés: Las pequeñas fisuras en el hueso suelen ser causadas por el uso excesivo.Fracturas en el tallo verde: son comunes en niños, en las que el hueso se dobla y se agrieta, pero no se rompe por completo.Fracturas conminutas: El hueso se rompe en varios pedazos.Fracturas compuestas (abiertas): el tipo más grave, en el que el hueso atraviesa la piel.Principales señales de que necesita atención médica inmediataSi no está seguro de la gravedad de su lesión, preste atención a estos síntomas de alerta. Si presenta alguno de ellos, debe consultar a un profesional de la salud de inmediato.Deformidad visible y huesos protuberantesEste es el signo más evidente de una fractura. Si una extremidad se ve torcida, forma un ángulo anormal o si se puede ver el hueso a través de una herida abierta, se trata de una emergencia médica.Según los NIH , una fractura abierta conlleva un alto riesgo de infección ósea profunda, que requiere limpieza quirúrgica inmediata y antibióticos.Hinchazón severa, hematomas e incapacidad para soportar peso.Si bien los esguinces causan hinchazón, una fractura ósea suele provocar hematomas intensos (equimosis) e hinchazón casi instantánea. Lo más importante es que, si no puede apoyar el pie afectado sin un dolor insoportable o si siente que el hueso está inestable, es muy probable que haya una fractura.Entumecimiento y hormigueoCuando un hueso se fractura, los bordes irregulares o la inflamación resultante pueden ejercer presión sobre los nervios cercanos.Según los NIH (Institutos Nacionales de la Salud de EE. UU .), si siente hormigueo, entumecimiento o sensación de frío en los dedos de las manos o de los pies cerca de la zona lesionada, esto indica que el flujo sanguíneo o la función nerviosa podrían estar comprometidos. Esto requiere intervención urgente para prevenir daños permanentes.Primeros auxilios: qué hacer al ir a urgenciasSi sospecha que se ha producido una rotura, su objetivo es minimizar los daños adicionales durante el transporte.El método RICE y la inmovilizaciónLos NIH (Institutos Nacionales de Salud de EE. UU.) indican que el protocolo estándar para lesiones agudas es el método RICE: Reposo, Hielo, Compresión y Elevación. Sin embargo, si un hueso está claramente fracturado, no intente enderezarlo.Inmovilizar: Utilice una férula (incluso un periódico enrollado o un trozo de madera) para evitar que la articulación por encima y por debajo de la lesión se mueva.Hielo: Aplique una bolsa fría envuelta en un paño durante 20 minutos para reducir la hinchazón.Para detener el sangrado: si la piel está rota, aplique una presión suave con un paño limpio.¿Por qué elegir una sala de urgencias independiente en lugar de un centro de atención de urgencias para lesiones óseas?Si bien los centros de atención de urgencias son excelentes para dolores de garganta o cortes menores, a menudo carecen de las herramientas de diagnóstico de alto nivel y del personal especializado necesarios para lesiones óseas complejas.La importancia de las radiografías y tomografías computarizadas inmediatas realizadas in situ.Según la FDA , la mayoría de las fracturas requieren pruebas de imagen para su confirmación. En nuestra sala de emergencias de White Rock, utilizamos tecnología de rayos X y tomografía computarizada de grado hospitalario.Esto permite a nuestros médicos observar la alineación exacta del hueso y detectar daños internos que una radiografía estándar podría pasar por alto. En un centro de atención de urgencias, es posible que lo deriven a otro lugar para realizarle pruebas de imagen, lo que le haría perder un tiempo valioso.Acceso a un manejo avanzado del dolorUna fractura es extremadamente dolorosa. Las salas de urgencias están equipadas para brindar un control avanzado del dolor y sedación que las clínicas de atención de urgencias no pueden ofrecer.Si es necesario recolocar un hueso, nuestro equipo puede brindar la comodidad necesaria para que el proceso sea lo menos doloroso posible.Qué esperar durante su visita a urgencias por una fracturaCuando llegue a nuestras instalaciones, nuestra prioridad será su estabilización.Clasificación inicial: Una enfermera evaluará rápidamente sus niveles de dolor y sus constantes vitales.Pruebas de imagen: Le trasladaremos a nuestra sala de radiografías.Examen físico: Un médico certificado revisará la función nerviosa y la circulación.Tratamiento: Dependiendo de la fractura, esto puede implicar una férula personalizada, un yeso o la derivación a un cirujano ortopédico si la fractura es compleja.Atención de seguimiento: Le proporcionamos instrucciones claras y referencias para garantizar que su hueso sane correctamente.Tratamiento rápido y compasivo de fracturas óseas en White Rock, Texas.No debería tener que esperar horas en una sala de espera de hospital abarrotada cuando siente dolor. En nuestro centro, nos enorgullecemos de brindar a la comunidad un tratamiento de alta calidad y eficiente para fracturas en la sala de emergencias de White Rock , Texas.Nuestro equipo combina la experiencia técnica de un hospital tradicional con la rapidez y el trato personalizado de una clínica de barrio.Acude ahora mismo a la sala de urgencias de White Rock para obtener un alivio rápido y atención especializada.¿Necesita atención inmediata? Llámenos ahora al (469) 943-2939Manténgase informado con consejos de salud de temporada, recomendaciones de primeros auxilios y maneras prácticas de cuidar su bienestar durante todo el año. Siga a ER of White Rock en Facebook e Instagram para obtener valiosas actualizaciones sobre salud. Preguntas frecuentes¿Cómo puedo saber si un hueso está roto sin una radiografía?Si bien síntomas como la deformidad, un sonido de «crujido» (crepitación) y la incapacidad para soportar peso son indicadores importantes, una radiografía es la única forma definitiva de diagnosticar una fractura y determinar su gravedad.¿Es una fractura peor que una rotura?No. En terminología médica, «fractura» y «rotura» son sinónimos. Sin embargo, el tipo de fractura (como una fisura fina o una fractura completa) determina la gravedad de la lesión.¿Puedo caminar con un pie roto?Es posible caminar con ciertos tipos de fracturas, como las fracturas por estrés o las roturas en huesos pequeños.¿Cuánto tiempo tarda en curarse un hueso roto?La mayoría de las fracturas tardan entre 6 y 8 semanas en curarse, aunque esto varía según la edad, el hueso afectado y el estado de salud general.¿Debo ir a urgencias por una lesión en un dedo de la mano o del pie?Si el dedo está torcido, entumecido o la uña está aplastada, debe acudir a urgencias. Las heridas en los dedos de las manos y los pies que no cicatrizan correctamente pueden provocar artritis crónica y pérdida de movilidad. text: Food Poisoning vs Stomach Bug: How to Tell the Difference and When to Get Emergency Care ER of White Rock Stomach and Digestive Medically reviewed by the ER of White Rock Nursing Team |Updated: July 22, 2026 Table of Contents It’s a situation most of us have faced: one minute you’re enjoying a great meal, and a few hours later, you’re doubled over in pain. When your stomach is in knots, the last thing you want to do is play detective. Is it just a “24-hour bug” going around the office, or is it something more serious that requires a trip to an emergency room near White Rock?Distinguishing between a common stomach virus (gastroenteritis) and food poisoning is more than just academic. It is about knowing when your body can recover at home and when you need emergency care for severe stomach pain to prevent life-threatening complications.What Causes Food Poisoning: Common Bacteria and VirusesAccording to MedlinePlus, food poisoning occurs when you consume food or water contaminated with bacteria, viruses, or parasites.A “stomach bug” is typically a viral infection passed from person to person. Food poisoning is a direct result of how food is handled, cooked, or stored.Incubation Times: The Most Useful Clue to Identify the Source MealThe CDC estimates that 48 million people get sick from foodborne illnesses each year. The time between eating the contaminated food and feeling symptoms (the incubation period) varies by pathogen, and knowing it helps you identify which meal caused the problem:Norovirus: 12 to 48 hours. The leading cause of foodborne illness in the US (responsible for about 58% of cases per the CDC). Spreads fast through close contact or contaminated surfaces.Salmonella: 6 hours to 6 days. Often found in undercooked poultry, eggs, or unpasteurized dairy.E. coli (O157 strain): 3 to 4 days. Frequently linked to undercooked ground beef or contaminated raw produce (spinach, romaine). Some strains cause severe kidney damage.Listeria: 1 to 90 days (often 1 to 4 weeks). Deli meats, soft cheeses made with raw milk, hot dogs that have not been reheated. Especially dangerous in pregnancy.Bacillus cereus: 30 minutes to 6 hours for the vomiting form (reheated rice, starchy foods left at room temperature). Classic clue: sickness right after a buffet or leftovers.If every family member who ate the same meal gets sick in a similar time window, the shared dish is the likely source. If only one person gets sick, look at a different origin (person-to-person contact, a different meal).The Standard Symptoms of Foodborne IllnessMost cases of food poisoning follow a predictable, if miserable, path. For many healthy adults, the body is remarkably good at flushing out these toxins on its own.Nausea, Vomiting, and Abdominal CrampingAccording to the CDC, the most common symptoms include nausea, projectile vomiting, and diarrhea. You may also experience:Intense stomach cramps as your muscles contract to expel the pathogenA low-grade fever and general “chills”Loss of appetite and fatigueThese symptoms are exhausting but usually manageable at home with rest and small sips of water or electrolyte drinks. When the symptoms escalate, you may need emergency treatment.Red Flags: When Food Poisoning Becomes a Medical EmergencyIt can be hard to decide whether to wait it out or head to the ER. If you cannot keep liquids down for more than a few hours, the situation has likely shifted from “nuisance” to “medical emergency.”Recognizing Severe DehydrationDehydration is the primary reason patients seek treatment for severe food poisoning. When you lose fluids through vomiting and diarrhea faster than you can replace them, your organs begin to struggle.MedlinePlus lists critical dehydration signs:Extreme thirst and a very dry mouthDark-colored urine or not urinating at all for 8+ hoursDizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting when trying to standSunken eyes or a rapid heart rateHigh Fever, Bloody Stools, and Vision ChangesSome symptoms indicate that the infection has moved beyond the digestive tract or is causing internal damage. Seek immediate emergency care if you notice:Bloody stools: can indicate severe inflammation or an infection like E. coli or ShigellaHigh fever: a temperature above 102°F (38.9°C) often suggests a more aggressive bacterial infectionNeurological symptoms: blurry vision, muscle weakness, or tingling in the arms can be signs of botulism, a rare but deadly form of food poisoningSymptoms Lasting Longer Than 48 HoursMost foodborne illnesses resolve within 12 to 48 hours. If your symptoms are not improving after two full days, your body may be losing the fight, and medical intervention is necessary to prevent long-term complications.At-Risk Groups Who Should Seek Immediate CareCertain people have a much lower threshold for complications. If you or a loved one falls into these categories, do not “wait and see”:Adults 65 and older: NIH states the immune system and kidneys do not recover as quickly from dehydration.Children under 5: small bodies lose fluid rapidly; dehydration in toddlers can become critical in hours.Pregnant women: infections like Listeria can be dangerous for the baby even when the mother does not feel that sick. The CDC recommends avoiding soft cheeses made with unpasteurized milk, deli meats, and hot dogs that have not been reheated during pregnancy.Immunocompromised individuals: patients on chemotherapy or living with chronic conditions like diabetes or HIV/AIDS.How the ER Diagnoses and Treats Food PoisoningWhen you arrive at our ER near White Rock with severe symptoms, the goal is twofold: stabilize your vitals and identify the cause.Rapid IV Fluid Hydration and Anti-Nausea MedicationsThe most immediate treatment for severe food poisoning is intravenous (IV) rehydration. This bypasses the stomach entirely, delivering fluids and essential electrolytes (sodium, potassium) directly into your bloodstream.Doctors also administer IV antiemetics (anti-nausea meds) to stop the vomiting cycle, allowing your body to rest.The Lab Panel We Actually RunTo determine whether you need specific antibiotics and to catch sepsis early, the team may run:Stool tests: a multiplex GI panel can identify 22 common pathogens from one sample.Complete blood count (CBC): high white blood cell counts suggest active bacterial infection.Metabolic panel (BUN, creatinine, electrolytes): checks kidney function and the sodium and potassium lost through vomiting and diarrhea.Lactate level: an elevated lactate is an early signal that the infection may be progressing to sepsis, and it triggers more aggressive fluid resuscitation and broad-spectrum antibiotics.Our on-site lab turns these results around in under 30 minutes, which matters when an infection is moving fast.The BRAT Diet: Why Current Guidelines Have Moved OnFor years, the BRAT diet (bananas, rice, applesauce, toast) was the standard first recommendation for returning to food after a stomach bug.Current pediatric guidance, including from the American Academy of Pediatrics at HealthyChildren.org, has moved away from BRAT as a strict prescription. It is too restrictive, low in protein and fat, and can prolong nutritional recovery, especially in children.The current recommendation is to return to a balanced normal diet as soon as the patient tolerates it, alongside oral rehydration solution (ORS) such as Pedialyte. Clear liquids and bland foods are fine in the first few hours, but enforcing BRAT for days is not evidence-based.Get Rapid Treatment for Severe Food Poisoning Near White RockYou do not have to suffer through severe dehydration alone. If you are experiencing persistent vomiting, high fever, or signs of dehydration, the ER of White Rock team is ready to help you recover quickly and safely.Visit ER of White Rock now for fast relief and expert care.Need Immediate Care? Call us now at (469) 943-2939.Stay informed with seasonal health tips, first-aid advice, and practical ways to maintain your well-being year-round. Follow ER of White Rock on Facebook and Instagram for health updates.FAQsHow long does food poisoning usually last?Most cases resolve within 24 to 48 hours. Depending on the bacteria (like Salmonella or Listeria), it can take several days or even weeks to feel fully back to normal.Can I take over-the-counter anti-diarrheal meds?Consult a doctor first. If the infection is bacterial, stopping the diarrhea can sometimes “trap” the toxins in your system longer and worsen the illness.What is the fastest way to recover from food poisoning?Rest and rehydration with oral rehydration solution (ORS) like Pedialyte. Current guidelines have moved away from the strict BRAT diet. Return to a balanced normal diet as your body tolerates it, in small frequent portions.When should I take my child to the ER for a stomach bug?If they have a dry diaper for more than 8 hours, lack tears when crying, are unusually lethargic, or vomiting and diarrhea have not resolved in 24 hours, seek emergency care immediately.Is food poisoning contagious?The food itself is not contagious, but the germs (like Norovirus) can spread through close contact or shared surfaces. Norovirus is notoriously hard to kill; alcohol-based hand sanitizer does not work on it. Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds.Will I need antibiotics for food poisoning?Not always.Most food poisoning is viral or clears on its own. Antibiotics are only prescribed for specific bacterial infections confirmed by a lab test. Empirical antibiotics in suspected E. coli O157 cases can actually raise the risk of hemolytic uremic syndrome, which is why we wait for the test result before treating.Latest Insights: What to Tell the ER Team: A Medication and Symptom Note Read More ... text: The Complete Parent’s Guide to Pediatric Emergencies: When to Take Your Child to the ER ER of White Rock Pediatric Care Medically reviewed by the ER of White Rock Nursing Team |Updated: August 19, 2026 Table of Contents It is 2 a.m. Your child is flushed, breathing fast, and you are standing in the hallway with a thermometer in your hand.The question pounding in your head is simple. Is this an emergency, or can it wait until morning?Every parent faces this moment. The fear is real, and the answer is rarely obvious from the couch. This guide is written to give you a clear way to think it through, even when you are scared and tired.At ER of White Rock, we are an independent freestanding emergency room open 24/7 at 10705 Northwest Hwy. We treat children every day from White Rock Lake, Lake Highlands, Casa View, Lakewood, Forest Hills, and East Dallas.The pages that follow walk through the warning signs, the conditions we treat, what to expect when you arrive, and when a different setting is the better call.How to Tell a Real Pediatric Emergency from Something That Can WaitChildren are not small adults. Their warning signs can look subtle, then escalate fast. A reliable rule of thumb is to focus on breathing, color, alertness, and hydration.If any of these four are clearly off, treat it as an emergency. Trust the pattern, not a single number on a thermometer.Red-Flag Symptoms That Need the ER NowSome symptoms should always send you straight in. Call 911 if your child is unresponsive, has stopped breathing, or is having a seizure that lasts longer than five minutes.Trouble breathing, ribs sucking in with each breath, or pauses between breathsBluish lips, fingernails, or skin that looks grayA fever in a baby under 3 months, or a fever with a stiff neck, severe headache, or a rash that does not fade when pressedA head injury followed by vomiting, confusion, or a brief loss of consciousnessSevere allergic reaction with swelling of the face, lips, or tongueDehydration with no wet diapers for 8 hours, sunken eyes, or no tears when cryingA first-time seizure, or any seizure in a child without a known seizure disorderSudden, severe abdominal pain, or vomiting that contains green bile or bloodSymptoms That Usually Can Wait for the PediatricianNot every fever or scrape needs an ER. A mild cough, a runny nose, an ear pull, or a low-grade fever in an otherwise active child can usually wait for a daytime call to the pediatrician.Most pediatric offices have an after-hours nurse line. They can listen to symptoms over the phone and tell you whether to come in, head to urgent care, or go to the ER.When you are not sure, calling them first costs you nothing and often saves a long night.Common Pediatric Emergencies We Treat at ER of White RockOur team is made up of experienced emergency medicine physicians and nurses who treat children alongside adults every day. We are not a children’s hospital, and we do not pretend to be.We are the right place for the conditions below, and we explain when we are not. Our pediatric care service page covers more on our approach.High Fever in ChildrenFever itself is not the enemy. It is the body’s way of fighting infection, and the temperature number alone is rarely the most important detail. The real question is how your child looks and acts.The American Academy of Pediatrics breaks the thresholds down by age, and those tiers are decision points the ER team uses too:Under 3 months: any rectal temperature of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher is an emergency. The newborn immune system cannot contain serious infections, and the source has to be identified fast.3 to 6 months: a fever of 102°F (38.9°C) or higher needs a same-day pediatrician call.6 months and older: behavior, hydration, and response to antipyretics matter more than the exact number. A child with a 103°F fever who is still playing and drinking is in better shape than one with 101°F who is lethargic and refusing fluids.Any fever paired with a stiff neck, severe headache, non-blanching rash, confusion, or extreme sleepiness crosses into ER territory regardless of age.Our team can run rapid labs, urine tests, and imaging on site to find the source. MedlinePlus has a useful overview of when childhood fevers cross from routine into urgent.For step-by-step symptom guidance, our high fever in children page goes deeper.Head Injury and Concussion in KidsBumps and tumbles are a normal part of childhood. Most do not need an ER. The injuries that do are the ones that come with warning signs in the minutes and hours afterward.Bring your child in if they lost consciousness for any length of time, vomited more than once, became unusually drowsy, slurred their words, had a seizure, or cannot remember what happened.The CDC HEADS UP program lists the full set of red flags every parent should know. Research summarized by the NIH reinforces that even mild traumatic brain injury in children deserves prompt evaluation.We can perform CT imaging on site within minutes when it is needed. For details on our evaluation pathway, see our emergency head injury and pediatric concussion treatment pages.Breathing Problems: Croup, Asthma, and RSVRespiratory illness is the single most common reason kids end up in our waiting room from October through March. Watch for the signs that breathing has become work, not just noisy.Retractions, where the skin pulls in around the ribs, collarbones, or the soft spot at the base of the neck, mean your child is using extra muscles to move air.A barking cough that gets worse at night can be croup. Wheezing that does not respond to a rescue inhaler can be a serious asthma flare.RSV deserves its own note. In babies under 12 months, RSV can cause rapid, shallow breathing, poor feeding, and dehydration.The American Academy of Pediatrics resource at HealthyChildren.org has plain-language guidance on respiratory red flags. If your child is struggling to breathe, do not wait.Our emergency care for breathing problems page explains how we evaluate and treat respiratory distress on arrival.Severe Dehydration in Babies and ToddlersA stomach bug in an adult is unpleasant. In an infant, it can become dangerous in under a day. Smaller bodies hold smaller fluid reserves.Watch for a dry mouth, no tears when crying, a sunken soft spot on a baby’s head, and no wet diaper for 6 to 8 hours. Older kids may complain of dizziness when they stand or feel weak and floppy.We start IV fluids quickly when oral rehydration is not working. Our dehydration treatment page walks through how we approach pediatric fluid replacement.Severe Allergic Reactions and AnaphylaxisAn allergic reaction crosses into anaphylaxis when more than one body system is involved. A spreading hive on the arm is one thing. Hives plus swelling of the lips, plus throat tightness, plus vomiting is anaphylaxis.Use the epinephrine auto-injector first if you have one. Then come straight to the ER, even if your child seems better.A second-wave reaction can hit hours later, which is why observation is part of the standard of care. MedlinePlus emphasizes that epinephrine is the first-line treatment and that medical follow-up is essential after any auto-injector use.The MedlinePlus anaphylaxis overview covers what to look for and why follow-up matters. If hives are the only symptom and your child is otherwise comfortable, our rashes treatment page covers when a rash needs urgent evaluation.Choking and Foreign Body IngestionIf your child is choking and cannot cough, cry, or speak, call 911 and start back blows for infants or abdominal thrusts for older children. If they are coughing forcefully, let them keep coughing.A strong cough is the best way to clear an airway.Swallowed objects are a different category. Small smooth items often pass on their own.Button batteries, magnets, and sharp objects are emergencies. A button battery lodged in the esophagus can cause tissue damage within two hours.If you suspect a button battery or magnet ingestion, come in immediately. We can locate the object on X-ray and coordinate transfer for endoscopic removal when needed.Seizures in ChildrenA first seizure is terrifying to witness. Place your child on their side, clear hard objects out of the way, do not put anything in their mouth, and time it.Call 911 if the seizure lasts longer than five minutes, if a second seizure follows immediately, or if your child does not return to normal alertness within about 20 minutes after it stops.A simple febrile seizure in a young child with a fever is more common than parents realize. The AAP defines a simple febrile seizure by three features: it lasts under 15 minutes, it is generalized (not focused on one body part), and it occurs only once in a 24-hour period. Simple febrile seizures do not increase epilepsy risk and do not require routine imaging or EEG, though every first seizure still deserves clinical evaluation.Complex febrile seizures (over 15 minutes, focal, or repeating within 24 hours) need a deeper workup to rule out meningitis or other serious causes.Eye injuries from playground falls, foreign objects, or chemical splashes are another time-sensitive concern. Our pediatric eye injury page explains when to come in versus rinse at home.What to Expect at a Freestanding ER for Your ChildMost parents picture an ER as a busy hospital lobby with a long wait. A freestanding emergency room is a different setting, and the differences matter when you have a sick or hurt child.We are open 24 hours a day, every day of the year. Wait times are typically much shorter than at hospital ERs because we do not share resources with inpatient floors or trauma services.Most patients are roomed within minutes of arrival.The Visit, Step by StepWhen you walk in, registration takes a few minutes. A nurse takes vital signs and asks about symptoms while a physician is paged.From there, the path depends on what is going on. We have on-site CT, X-ray, ultrasound, and a full lab.That means most diagnostic answers come back in 30 to 60 minutes rather than hours. Treatment, whether it is IV fluids, a breathing treatment, stitches, or fracture care, starts the moment we know what we are dealing with.When We Stabilize and Refer: The Children’s Medical Center Dallas PathwayThis is the honest part. We are an emergency room, not a children’s hospital.If your child needs pediatric ICU admission, pediatric surgery, neonatal intensive care, or a pediatric subspecialist for a complex case, we are not the final destination.What we do in those situations is what every well-run ER does. We stabilize first. We start fluids, oxygen, medications, and any imaging that is needed.The usual destination for serious pediatric cases near White Rock is Children’s Medical Center Dallas, which the Texas Department of State Health Services has designated as a Level I Pediatric Trauma Center, the state’s highest tier. That designation means 24/7 pediatric surgery, pediatric neurosurgery, pediatric ICU, and neonatal ICU on-site. We coordinate transfer by ambulance with our team monitoring until handoff, and communicate directly with the receiving team before transport.The goal is that your child arrives there in better shape than they would have if you had driven across town yourself.When to Skip the ER: Pediatrician, Urgent Care, or Virtual VisitComing to the ER for a true emergency is the right call. Coming to the ER for a routine cold is not, and being honest about that helps families spend less and stress less.For routine concerns, your pediatrician is the right first call. Examples include well-child checks, immunizations, mild ear infections, common colds, low-grade fevers in older kids who are eating and playing, and follow-up on chronic conditions.Build a relationship with a pediatric office before you need one.What Urgent Care Handles WellUrgent care clinics fill the middle ground. They are a good fit for minor sprains, small lacerations that may need a few stitches, suspected strep throat, mild rashes, and uncomplicated UTIs in older children.They typically have shorter hours than a 24/7 ER and fewer diagnostic tools.Some families also use telehealth or virtual urgent care for non-emergent advice when the pediatrician’s office is closed. That can be a reasonable bridge for triage, though it is not a substitute for hands-on evaluation when symptoms are concerning.The Bottom Line on SettingIf breathing, color, alertness, or hydration is clearly off, the ER is the right setting. If symptoms are mild and your child is acting like themselves, start with the pediatrician’s after-hours line.When in doubt, call. Triage advice from a nurse you trust is one of the most underused tools parents have.How to Prepare Your Family for a Pediatric EmergencyThe best time to plan for an ER visit is before you need one. A few small steps make a stressful night much smoother.Save your insurance card image and your pediatrician’s after-hours number on your phoneKeep a current list of your child’s medications, doses, and allergies in a notes appKnow your child’s weight in kilograms or pounds (medication dosing is weight-based)Note any chronic conditions, recent surgeries, and the date of the last tetanus shotPack a small comfort item bag: a favorite stuffed animal, a blanket, a charged tablet with headphones, a snack for siblingsHave a backup childcare plan for siblings if you might need to leave the house quicklyMap the route to ER of White Rock from your home and have it saved offlineThe CDC’s Parents and Caregivers resources include broader emergency-readiness checklists for families. Even a 10-minute prep session can save a panicked search at 2 a.m.What to Tell Your Child on the WayKids absorb your tone more than your words. Stay calm, even if you have to fake it for a few minutes.Use simple, honest language about what will happen. Tell them the doctors and nurses help kids feel better.Let them hold a comfort item. Avoid promising “no shots”, because broken promises in the ER make the next visit harder.Serving Families in White Rock, Lake Highlands, and East DallasWe are minutes from White Rock Lake, the Lake Highlands schools corridor, Casa View, Casa Linda, Forest Hills, Lakewood, Old Lake Highlands, and the Garland border.Most families in our catchment can reach us in 10 to 15 minutes, which matters when a child is struggling to breathe, running a high fever, showing heat stroke warning signs on a Texas summer day, or being watched after a near-drowning at White Rock Lake.Our address is 10705 Northwest Hwy. We are open 24 hours a day, every day, including holidays.The phone number is (469) 943-2939, and you do not need an appointment.We accept most major private insurance plans, including Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, and UnitedHealthcare. Our front desk can verify your specific plan when you arrive, and we work with families on payment for any out-of-pocket portion.Frequently Asked QuestionsWhen should I take my child to the ER for a fever?Any fever in a baby under 3 months is an ER visit. For older children, come in if a fever is paired with a stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, a non-blanching rash, repeated vomiting, trouble breathing, or extreme sleepiness. The look of your child matters more than the number on the thermometer.Can a freestanding ER treat my baby?Yes. ER of White Rock evaluates and treats infants and children of all ages, 24 hours a day. We have pediatric-sized equipment, weight-based medication protocols, and on-site imaging and labs. For cases that need pediatric ICU, NICU, or pediatric surgery, we stabilize first and arrange transfer to Children’s Medical Center Dallas, the Texas DSHS-designated Level I Pediatric Trauma Center.Does a febrile seizure mean my child will have epilepsy?Simple febrile seizures (under 15 minutes, generalized, single in 24 hours) do not significantly raise epilepsy risk and are common in young children with a fever. Complex febrile seizures (longer, focal, or repeating) do warrant deeper workup. Even a first simple febrile seizure deserves ER evaluation to rule out meningitis, sepsis, or another serious cause of the fever itself.What insurance do you accept for pediatric visits?We accept most major private insurance plans, including Aetna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, Cigna, and UnitedHealthcare. Bring your insurance card and a photo ID. Our front desk verifies coverage at check-in and can answer questions about your specific plan.Should I drive my child or call 911?Call 911 if your child is unresponsive, not breathing, having a seizure that will not stop, or has a serious injury that should not be moved. Paramedics can start treatment in the ambulance. For most other emergencies, driving directly to ER of White Rock is appropriate, especially if you are within 10 to 15 minutes.What happens if my child needs surgery or pediatric ICU care?We stabilize the patient first, then coordinate transfer to a children’s hospital with the right specialty team. That includes IV access, oxygen, pain control, imaging, and constant monitoring. Our team stays with your child until handoff, and we communicate directly with the receiving hospital before transport.How long is the wait at ER of White Rock?Most patients are roomed within minutes of arrival. Because we are a freestanding ER, we do not share staff or rooms with hospital inpatient services. That is a major reason wait times are shorter than a typical hospital ER. Critical cases are seen first.Is the ER safe during cold and flu season?Yes. We use separate evaluation rooms, source control with masking when respiratory illness is circulating, and frequent surface cleaning. If you are worried about exposure, mention it at check-in and we can adjust your child’s room placement.If You Are Worried Right NowTrust the instinct that brought you here. If your child’s breathing, color, alertness, or hydration looks off, head to ER of White Rock at 10705 Northwest Hwy or call (469) 943-2939.We are open right now, and we have been here for families across White Rock, Lake Highlands, and East Dallas every hour of every day.Stay informed with seasonal health tips and first-aid guidance for parents. Call 911 Now Not breathing, severe bleeding, unresponsive, or signs of stroke or heart attack. Do not drive yourself. text: CARDIAC EMERGENCY CARE · 24/7 OPENChest Pain Treatment & Cardiac Emergency Care in White Rock, TXWhen chest pain hits, every minute counts. ER of White Rock delivers a 12-lead EKG in 5 minutes, hs-troponin during triage, and on-site CT imaging, with experienced ER physicians around the clock. Call 24/7: (469) 943-2939 Get Directions 12-lead EKG in 5 minutes Open 24/7 Experienced ER Physicians EMERGENCY TRIAGEIs This an Emergency? When Chest Pain Means Call 911 NowThe American Heart Association and ACEP classify these warning signs as immediately life-threatening. If you notice any of them, call 911 right away. Do not drive yourself.EMS can start aspirin, oxygen, and a 12-lead EKG before you reach the ER. They alert our team to your arrival so triage begins the moment you walk in. Pressure or tightness > 15 minutes Classic ischemic chest discomfort that doesn't ease with rest. AHA. Pain radiating to jaw, arm, neck, or back Referred pain is a hallmark of myocardial infarction. AHA. Sudden severe shortness of breath May indicate pulmonary embolism, MI, or aortic dissection. ACEP. Cold sweat with chest pain Autonomic response with high predictive value for heart attack. AHA. Light-headedness, dizziness, or fainting Possible arrhythmia or reduced cardiac output. AHA. Weakness or numbness on one side of body Stroke can present with chest pain in atypical cases. CDC.Call 911 immediately if you experience any of these signs. Don’t drive yourself. EMS can start treatment on the way to the ER. CONDITIONS WE EVALUATEWhat Causes Chest Pain? Six Conditions We Rule In or OutNot every chest pain is a heart attack, but our team rules out the dangerous cardiovascular causes first. The differential below runs in order of urgency, starting with conditions that become fatal within minutes if missed.Blood clots in the lung and aortic dissection can both present as chest pain. Stroke-related pain in the neck or jaw also triggers the same triage protocol. Heart Attack (STEMI / NSTEMI) 12-lead EKG within 5 minutes plus hs-troponin in triage flag a heart attack. STEMI activates the cath lab immediately. AHA. Unstable Angina Chest pain at rest or with minimal exertion, even with negative troponin, signals high-risk coronary disease. HEART score guides admission. AHA. Pulmonary Embolism Sudden shortness of breath with chest pain. We use Wells score, D-dimer, and CT pulmonary angiogram to rule it in or out. ACEP. Aortic Dissection Sudden tearing chest or back pain. CT angiogram of the chest rules it in or out. Time-critical. ACEP. Pericarditis & Myocarditis Sharp positional pain, EKG changes, and bedside echo identify pericardial inflammation. NIH. Non-Cardiac Causes GERD, musculoskeletal strain, and anxiety can mimic cardiac symptoms. We rule out heart causes first, every time. AHA. RISK FACTORSWho Is at Highest Risk for Cardiac Chest Pain?Knowing your risk changes how we work up your chest pain. The more factors that apply, the lower our threshold for advanced cardiac testing like serial troponin or stress imaging.Roughly half of U.S. adults have hypertension per CDC data, and a third have abnormal cholesterol. Chest pain in the over-40 group with even one risk factor gets the full workup by default.KEY RISK FACTORS Age (45+ men / 55+ women) Risk doubles each decade. AHA. Hypertension ≥130/80 2017 ACC/AHA threshold for stage 1 hypertension. High LDL Cholesterol ≥100 mg/dL NHLBI guideline for primary prevention. Diabetes HbA1c ≥6.5% ADA diagnostic threshold for type 2 diabetes. Smoking or Vaping Smokers face roughly 3x MI risk vs non-smokers. AHA. Family History of MI First-degree relative with MI before 55 (men) or 65 (women). AHA.BY THE NUMBERS 805Kheart attacks per yearCDC 1 in 5heart attacks are silentCDC 47%U.S. adults with hypertensionCDC #1leading cause of death in U.S.CDC ATYPICAL PRESENTATIONSWhy Does Chest Pain Look Different in Women, Diabetics, and Older Adults?Up to 38% of women, 25% of people with diabetes, and nearly half of older adults can have a heart attack without classic chest pressure. MedlinePlus documents jaw pain, back pain between the shoulder blades, sudden fatigue, and nausea as common atypical presentations. Recognizing these patterns at triage is what prevents a missed MI in the very groups most likely to have one. WOMEN Classic chest pressure may be absent. We watch for: Nausea or indigestion Unusual fatigue (often days before) Shortness of breath Jaw, back, or neck pain Cold sweat without chest pressureSource: AHA Go Red for Women / NEJM PEOPLE WITH DIABETES Autonomic neuropathy can blunt pain. We watch for: Shortness of breath without obvious pain Sudden severe fatigue or weakness Hypotension or light-headedness Mild upper-abdominal discomfort New unexplained sweatingSource: ADA / AHA ADULTS 65+ Atypical presentation is common at older ages: New confusion or altered mental state Syncope or unexplained fall Shortness of breath without chest pain Sudden severe weakness Abdominal pain mimicking GI illnessSource: ACC / NHLBI OUR WORKUP PROCESSWhat We Look For in Your Chest Pain WorkupTime matters. Every step of the workup below is timed to ACC and ACEP standards.We deliver a 12-lead EKG within 5 minutes and hs-troponin during triage rather than after wait. On-site CT imaging and lab are available if the picture is unclear. The goal: rule in or rule out the highest-risk conditions before you sit down. 01TRIAGE · 0–2 MINBrief Triage and VitalsPulse, BP, SpO2, focused history, and IV access primed. Chief complaint logged so the cath lab can be on standby if STEMI activates downstream. ACEP. 02EKG · ≤ 5 MIN · ACC STANDARD12-Lead EKGRead at the bedside by an ER physician. ST-elevation activates the cath lab immediately. ACC door-to-EKG target is 10 minutes; our internal target is 5. 03TROPONIN · 5–10 MINHigh-Sensitivity TroponinFirst hs-troponin drawn at triage. If positive or rising, NSTEMI workup begins immediately. Repeat at 1 and 3 hours per ESC 0/1/3 algorithm. 04IMAGING · 15–30 MINChest X-Ray and Targeted CTChest X-ray for every chest pain. CT pulmonary angiogram if PE suspected (Wells score). CT angiogram of chest if aortic dissection suspected. ACEP. 05DECISION · 30–60 MINHEART Score and DispositionHEART score combines history, EKG, age, risk factors, and troponin. Score ≥7 admits. 4 to 6 observation. 0 to 3 home with cardiology follow-up. AHA/ACC pathway. WHERE TO GO FOR CHEST PAINShould I Go to the ER, Urgent Care, or Cardiologist for Chest Pain?Chest pain is one of the few symptoms where venue choice can change outcome. Urgent care cannot run hs-troponin or interpret an EKG against ACC criteria. A cardiologist’s office cannot admit you if the EKG looks bad.Only an emergency room can do all three: rule out infarction in real time, stabilize, and bridge to admission or discharge with a confirmed answer. Emergency Room (ER) Best forSevere, sudden, or red-flag chest painWait timeTriage in minutes, EKG in 5Can do12-lead EKG, hs-troponin, CT, cath lab activationEMTALA federal screening, no out-of-pocket for evaluation. Urgent Care Best forMild non-cardiac chest discomfortWait time30 to 90 minutes typicalCan doVitals and basic EKG if availableMust refer you to the ER if EKG is abnormal. Cardiologist Office Best forEstablished follow-up, chronic stable symptomsWait timeDays to weeks for an appointmentCan doStress test, echo, holter, medication managementNot equipped for emergency presentations. FREESTANDING ER ADVANTAGESWhy Choose a Freestanding ER Over a Hospital ER for Chest Pain?ER of White Rock is a full-capability freestanding emergency room. For chest pain, minutes change outcomes.We keep a 12-lead EKG, hs-troponin, and CT under one roof 24/7, with experienced emergency physicians on every shift. Your door-to-EKG time is measured in minutes. FASTER DOOR-TO-EKG Triage in minutes, EKG in 5, versus the 60-plus minute door-to-EKG common at busy hospital ERs during peak hours. ACC. SAME EQUIPMENT 12-lead EKG, high-sensitivity troponin, CT chest, CT angiogram, and cath lab activation pathway. BOARD-CERTIFIED ER MDs Every shift staffed by ABEM- or AAEM-certified emergency physicians. ACEP standard. NO TRAUMA QUEUE Hospital ER trauma cases override chest-pain workflow. Our freestanding ER is chest-pain-first. FREQUENTLY ASKEDCommon Questions About Chest Pain and the ER WorkupThe eight questions below answer the most-searched chest-pain queries with the same clinical detail we use at the bedside. Each answer is brief by design so a reader can grab the headline in 10 seconds, and longer if you tap to expand.If your specific question is not covered, walk in or call (469) 943-2939 and ask the on-shift physician directly. How long does a chest pain workup take in the ER?A standard chest pain workup at ER of White Rock takes 30 to 60 minutes from arrival to disposition. Triage and 12-lead EKG happen in the first 5 minutes. Troponin draws and imaging follow. The HEART score guides whether you go home, observe, or admit. ACEP. What does an EKG check for?A 12-lead EKG records the heart’s electrical activity from 12 angles. ER physicians read it at the bedside to detect ST-elevation (active heart attack), arrhythmias, conduction blocks, and signs of previous MI. STEMI on EKG triggers immediate cath lab activation. ACC. What is troponin and why is it important?Troponin is a protein released by injured heart muscle. High-sensitivity troponin can detect a heart attack within 1 to 3 hours of symptom onset. A negative high-sensitivity troponin at 0 and 3 hours can safely rule out MI in most patients. ESC. Can stress or anxiety cause chest pain that feels like a heart attack?Yes. Panic and severe anxiety can produce chest tightness, shortness of breath, and even arm numbness that mimics a heart attack. We rule out cardiac causes first with EKG and troponin before attributing pain to anxiety. AHA. Is chest pain always a sign of a heart attack?No. Common non-cardiac chest pain causes include GERD, musculoskeletal strain, pleurisy, and anxiety. However, only an ER workup can rule out cardiac causes with certainty. ACEP guidance is to evaluate every chest pain in the ER first. ACEP. How long after a heart attack does troponin show up in blood?High-sensitivity troponin can be detected within 1 to 3 hours of MI onset. Older troponin assays took 6 to 12 hours. ER of White Rock uses high-sensitivity assays so we can rule out MI faster, often within 3 hours of arrival. ESC. When should I worry about chest pain that comes and goes?Intermittent chest pain that recurs over hours or days, especially with exertion, can signal unstable angina, a warning sign before a heart attack. Do not wait for the pain to become constant. Come in for evaluation. AHA. Can heartburn feel like a heart attack?Yes. GERD and heart attacks can present with similar burning chest pressure. The safest path is to come in and let an EKG and troponin rule out cardiac causes. Antacids relieving the pain does not confirm GERD over a heart attack. AHA. FIND USConveniently Located for White Rock, Lake Highlands & East Dallas ER of White Rock 10705 Northwest Hwy, Dallas, TX 75238 (469) 943-2939 Open 24/7, no appointment needed Get Directions SERVING THESE NEIGHBORHOODS White Rock Lake Lake Highlands Lakewood M Streets Casa View INSURANCE & COVERAGEInsurance & Patient ProtectionsYou are protected by two federal laws when you come to a freestanding ER for chest pain. These protections apply even if you are uninsured or out-of-network.EMTALA guarantees screening and stabilization regardless of ability to pay. The No Surprises Act caps out-of-network charges to your in-network deductible and copay. EMTALA PROTECTION Federal law requires every ER to medically screen and stabilize you for an emergency condition before any insurance question. Applies even if you are uninsured. NO SURPRISES ACT For emergency care, you pay no more than your in-network cost-sharing even when the facility or provider is out-of-network. COMMERCIAL PLANS ACCEPTED We work with most major commercial insurance plans. Call our billing team to verify in-network status before non-emergency visits.Note: ER of White Rock is a freestanding emergency room. We are not a participating provider in any state or federal health care program, including Medicare, Medicaid, Tricare, VA Health, CHAMPVA, and the Indian Health Service. For all other coverage questions, call (469) 943-2939. RELATED CONDITIONSOther Cardiac & Respiratory Emergencies We TreatChest pain often overlaps with these four conditions. They are the most common co-presentations we evaluate alongside a cardiac workup. If your symptoms point to any of them, we work up and treat all of them under the same roof, 24/7. Many patients also need workup for conditions outside the heart and lungs. text: Emergency Stroke Care and Evaluation in White Rock, TXWhen a stroke happens, every single minute determines your brain health and recovery. At ER of White Rock, our 24/7 freestanding emergency room provides immediate, life-saving evaluations for severe stroke symptoms. We utilize advanced on-site CT imaging to determine if you are experiencing a blood clot or a brain bleed. Our experienced emergency physicians are ready to stabilize your condition with minimal wait times right here in East Dallas.Get Immediate Emergency Stroke Care NowHow to Recognize a Stroke: Act F.A.S.T.A stroke is a critical medical emergency that cuts off blood flow to the brain. Recognizing the warning signs early can save a life. The CDC recommends the F.A.S.T. method to identify a stroke:Face Drooping: Does one side of the face droop or feel completely numb?Arm Weakness: Ask the person to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?Speech Difficulty: Is their speech suddenly slurred or impossible to understand?Time to Call 911: If you observe any of these signs, seek emergency stroke care immediately.Mini strokes, clinically known as transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), produce similar symptoms and are a massive warning sign of a future stroke. Risk factors like high blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking drastically increase your chances of a neurological event. Do not ignore these symptoms.Our stroke evaluation at ER of White Rock includes immediate diagnostic imaging, vital sign stabilization, and coordination of thrombolytic therapies for ischemic and hemorrhagic strokes.Stroke recognition is one piece of broader cardiovascular awareness. Our cardiovascular emergencies guide near White Rock covers heart attack, stroke, and blood clot warning signs. Call Us Now Why Choose ER of White Rock for Stroke Emergencies? 24/7 Rapid Triage 24/7 Rapid Triage Stroke emergencies do not wait for business hours. Our doors are always open, ensuring you completely bypass the standard hospital waiting room for immediate medical attention. Advanced CT Imaging Advanced CT Imaging We feature state-of-the-art CT scanners on-site to instantly look inside the brain. This allows our team to quickly diagnose whether you have an ischemic stroke or a hemorrhagic stroke. Expert Emergency Physicians Expert Emergency Physicians Our experienced emergency doctors specialize in rapid neurological assessments and initial stroke stabilization protocols to help minimize long-term brain damage. Clot-Busting Medication Coordination Clot-Busting Medication Coordination For ischemic strokes, time is critical. We quickly assess your eligibility for life-saving thrombolytic therapies to break up dangerous brain clots. Seamless Specialist Transfers Seamless Specialist Transfers Once stabilized, we coordinate direct medical transport to the highest-rated comprehensive stroke centers in Dallas for advanced neurosurgery or ongoing neurological care.Understanding Your Stroke Risk FactorsWhile our East Dallas facility is here to provide life-saving care, understanding stroke prevention is just as important for protecting your family. The NIH NINDS identifies high blood pressure as the leading cause of strokes and brain bleeds. If you or a loved one have a history of hypertension, taking proactive steps is vital:Manage Blood Pressure: Check your levels regularly and take all prescribed medications.Control Diabetes: High blood sugar damages blood vessels over time and increases clot risks.Quit Smoking: Smoking thickens your blood and drastically increases the chance of plaque buildup.Watch for Warning Signs: Sudden dizziness, severe unexplained headaches, or temporary vision loss are warning signs that require an immediate ER evaluation. Get Direction What to Do If You Suspect a Brain Bleed or StrokeIf you or a family member show signs of a stroke, take these exact steps to ensure the best possible medical outcome:Note the Exact Time: Look at the clock the moment symptoms begin. This critical detail dictates which medications our doctors can safely use.Keep the Patient Awake: Do not let them go to sleep to see if the symptoms pass. Keep them alert.Do Not Give Aspirin or Food: If they are having a brain bleed, blood thinners like aspirin can be fatal. If their throat muscles are affected, food or water can cause choking.Act Immediately: Call 911 or drive directly to our Dallas emergency room. Get Immediate Care Now ER of White Rock: Your Trusted Stroke Care ProviderAt ER of White Rock, we are committed to delivering top-tier initial stroke care in Dallas, Texas. Our rapid-response team, advanced diagnostic technology, and coordinated specialist referrals ensure that every patient receives immediate assessment and highly accurate care coordination. Infant Under 3 Months with Fever Any temp 100.4 F or higher.Walk in 24/7 or call (469) 943-2939. We triage every fever immediately. CAUSES & DIAGNOSISWhat Causes a High Fever?Every fever workup screens for these six time-sensitive causes first. Physical exam, labs, and imaging confirm or rule out each, usually within 60-90 minutes. Sepsis Confirmed by blood culture and lactate. IV fluids plus broad-spectrum antibiotics within the first hour. Pneumonia Chest X-ray on arrival confirms or excludes. Severity scored to decide treat-and-release or admit. Kidney Infection Flank pain or back tenderness plus fever. Urinalysis confirms; IV antibiotics start on the spot. Meningitis Stiff neck, severe headache, or altered mental status. Lumbar puncture and antibiotics within 30 minutes. Flu & COVID-19 Rapid antigen and PCR in-house. Antivirals for high-risk patients during flu season. Appendicitis Right-lower-quadrant pain with fever. CT abdomen in 30 minutes; surgical consult from the bedside. BY THE NUMBERSWhy a Fever Workup MattersMost fevers resolve on their own; some hide serious infection. The numbers below are why our protocol treats every fever like sepsis-until-proven-otherwise. Aggressive screening saves lives. 270,000 Annual U.S. deaths from sepsis (CDC). Sepsis often starts as a fever and progresses fast. 8% / hour Sepsis survival drops about 8% for every hour antibiotics are delayed (Surviving Sepsis Campaign). 100.4 F Medical threshold for fever. In infants under 3 months, this alone is an ER emergency. 24 / 7 Experienced emergency physicians on every shift. No appointment, no overnight closure, no holiday gap.Sources: CDC Sepsis Data & Reports | Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 Guidelines POPULATIONS AT HIGHER RISKWhen Fever Is Always an Emergency: Three PopulationsFor three groups, fever presents differently and the trigger for ER evaluation is lower. The same temperature that means “rest and fluids” for a healthy adult means “workup now” for these patients. Knowing this distinction can save hours of dangerous delay. Infants 0-3 Months Any rectal temp 100.4 F or higher is an ER emergency, per AAP. Full sepsis workup is required: blood culture, urinalysis with culture, and often lumbar puncture. Their immune system cannot localize infection. Adults 65+ Older adults often run lower baseline temperatures. A fever 100 F or above with confusion, falls, or appetite loss can signal sepsis or pneumonia even without classic chills. Don't wait for textbook symptoms. Immunocompromised Patients on chemotherapy, biologics, post-transplant, or with HIV need ER evaluation for fever 100.4 F or higher. Neutropenic fever has narrow time-to-antibiotic windows. Bring a current medication list. OUR PROCESSWhat Happens During an ER Fever Workup?Every fever visit follows the same evidence-based workup. The order is dictated by national emergency-medicine standards (ACEP, AAP, Surviving Sepsis Campaign). Total door-to-decision time for most fever cases is 60-120 minutes. Critical cases (sepsis, infants) bypass the queue and start antibiotics in the first hour. Step 1: Triage 3-5 min check-in: temp, heart rate, respiratory rate. Sepsis screen runs automatically; high-risk patients bypass the waiting room. Step 2: Vitals & History Physician interview: onset, duration, exposures, immunization status, current meds. Full vitals trend started. Step 3: Labs CBC, CMP, blood cultures, lactate, urinalysis. Results in 30-60 minutes on-site, no outside lab transfer. Step 4: Imaging Chest X-ray, abdominal ultrasound, or CT scan as clinically indicated. Reading by an ED-trained radiologist within 30 min. Step 5: Disposition Treat-and-discharge with prescription, observe for 4-6 hours, or admit to a partner hospital. Clear written instructions and follow-up plan. No transfer to an outside reference lab, no transfer for imaging. CBC, blood cultures, lactate, urinalysis in 30-60 minutes CT, X-ray, ultrasound read by ED-trained radiologist Experienced emergency physicians on every shift DECISION GUIDEER or Urgent Care for a Fever?Not every fever needs an ER. When red-flag symptoms appear (see Section 2 above), the ER is the only correct answer. Emergency Room Choose ER when fever is 103+ F with stiff neck, confusion, trouble breathing, non-blanching rash, persistent vomiting, severe dehydration, OR for ANY infant under 3 months with temp 100.4+ F. Open 24/7, full labs + IV + imaging on-site. Urgent Care Choose urgent care for adults with mild fever under 102 F, mild flu-like symptoms, simple sore throat, no red flags. Limited lab capability; no IV antibiotics. Often closed nights, weekends, holidays. Primary Care / Pediatrician Best for established patients with low-grade fever, routine post-vaccine reactions, chronic-illness flares, or follow-up after an ER visit. Continuity of records; limited weekend access. FREESTANDING ER ADVANTAGESWhy Choose a Freestanding ER for Fever?ER of White Rock is a full-capability freestanding emergency room. For fever, especially in infants and immunocompromised patients, minutes change outcomes. We keep CBC, blood cultures, urinalysis, CT, and IV antibiotics under one roof on a 24/7 schedule, with experienced emergency physicians on every shift. Faster Door-to-Vitals Triage in 3-5 minutes. Hospital ERs average 30+ minutes before vitals because trauma cases bump the queue. On-Site Sepsis Labs CBC, blood cultures, lactate, and urinalysis all in the same visit. No transfer, no waiting for an outside reference lab. Pediatric + Adult Full pediatric workup capability from newborns onward. No referral to a separate children's facility for a fever screen. No Trauma Queue Your fever workup doesn't get bumped by gunshots, car wrecks, or stroke alerts. Every patient is your priority. FREQUENTLY ASKEDCommon Questions About High Fever and the ER WorkupThe eight questions below answer the most-searched fever queries with the same clinical detail we use at the bedside. Each answer is brief by design so you can grab the headline in 10 seconds, and longer if you tap to expand. If your specific question is not covered, walk in or call (469) 943-2939 and ask the on-shift physician directly. When should I take my child to the ER for a fever?Any infant under 3 months with a rectal temperature of 100.4 F or higher should go to the ER immediately, per AAP guidelines. When in doubt, walk in. We screen children 24/7. What temperature counts as a high fever?In adults, 100.4 F (38 C) is the medical threshold for fever; over 103 F (39.4 C) is high and warrants evaluation if it persists. In children under 3 months, anything 100.4 F or higher is a high fever requiring ER evaluation. Above 105 F at any age is a true emergency because brain function and organ stress accelerate above that threshold. How long should I wait before going to the ER for a fever?Do not wait if the fever comes with stiff neck, severe headache, confusion, trouble breathing, non-blanching rash, or signs of severe dehydration (no urine for 8+ hours, dry mouth, lethargy). Otherwise, an adult fever that persists above 103 F for more than 48-72 hours despite acetaminophen or ibuprofen deserves an ER workup to rule out sepsis, pneumonia, or kidney infection. text: Trusted Emergency Care for Blood ClotsBlood clots are common and frequently missed at home. The CDC estimates roughly 900,000 Americans develop venous thromboembolism (DVT or pulmonary embolism) every year, and 60,000 to 100,000 die from it. Pulmonary embolism is the third most common cardiovascular cause of death after heart attack and stroke (American Heart Association).If you live in the White Rock, Lake Highlands, or Lakewood area and you have one-sided leg swelling, sudden shortness of breath, sharp chest pain that worsens with deep breath, or unexplained fast heart rate, ER of White Rock evaluates and treats blood clots on site, 24/7.Blood clots fall under the broader scope of cardiovascular emergencies. Our cardiovascular emergencies guide near White Rock covers heart attack, stroke, and clot recognition together.Get Blood Clot Treatment TodayWhat Is a Blood Clot?A blood clot is a semi-solid mass of platelets, fibrin, and trapped red cells that forms inside a blood vessel. The body needs clotting to stop bleeding, but an abnormal clot in a deep vein or pulmonary artery blocks normal blood flow.The classic mechanism is described by Virchow’s triad: slowed blood flow (long flights, immobility after surgery), vessel injury, and increased clotting tendency (pregnancy, oral contraceptives, cancer, genetic factors like Factor V Leiden). Most people who form a clinically dangerous clot have at least two of these factors active at once.Two presentations matter most in the ER:Deep vein thrombosis (DVT): typically a clot in the calf, thigh, or pelvic vein. One-sided leg pain, swelling, and warmth.Pulmonary embolism (PE): a clot that has traveled to the lung. Sudden shortness of breath, sharp chest pain on inspiration, fast heart rate, sometimes cough with blood.Roughly one in three untreated proximal DVTs progresses to PE. That is why early evaluation matters. Call Us Now Symptoms That Require Immediate AttentionThe Wells score is the standard clinical decision rule emergency physicians use to estimate DVT and PE probability. The findings below are the ones that move the score the most.Come to ER of White Rock now if you have:One-sided leg pain, swelling, or tenderness, especially in the calf or thighWarmth, redness, or visible vein engorgement on the affected legSudden shortness of breath, especially at rest or with mild activitySharp chest pain that worsens when you breathe in (pleuritic chest pain)Fast heart rate (over 100 bpm) with no obvious causeCoughing up blood or pink-tinged sputumRecent risk factor: long flight or car trip over 6 hours, surgery in the past 4 weeks, pregnancy or postpartum within 6 weeks, cancer treatment, immobilization in a cast or bootCall 911 instead of driving if you are short of breath at rest, your lips or fingertips are turning blue, or you feel like you might pass out. Get Direction How we treat blood clots at ER of White RockAt ER of White Rock, we provide advanced diagnosis and treatment options for blood clots, ensuring rapid relief and preventing complications. Advanced Diagnostics Emergency Medical Interventions Preventive Care & Follow-Up Duplex ultrasound of the affected leg or arm to confirm DVT, done on site in 15 to 30 minutesCT pulmonary angiogram (CTPA) for suspected PE when the Wells score and d-dimer point to high probabilityD-dimer blood test with rapid turnaround (10 to 20 minutes) to rule out clot in low-probability patientsComplete coagulation panel (PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen) to baseline before starting anticoagulationEKG and troponin if PE is on the differential, since right-heart strain can mimic cardiac eventsPulse oximetry and arterial blood gas for patients with low oxygen saturationAnticoagulation started in the ER: heparin IV for hospital admissions, enoxaparin (Lovenox) injection for stable DVT discharges, or a direct oral anticoagulant (apixaban, rivaroxaban) when appropriate per CHEST 2021 guidelinesThrombolytic therapy (tPA) for massive or submassive PE with hemodynamic instability or significant right-heart strainOxygen and supportive care for PE patients with low oxygen saturationCatheter-directed thrombolysis or thrombectomy referral for severe iliofemoral DVT or PE with shock, coordinated with the receiving interventional teamIVC filter placement only for the narrow indication of recurrent clots despite anticoagulation or active major bleedingCompression stockings (15 to 20 mmHg for long flights or post-op, 20 to 30 mmHg if you have had a prior DVT)Move every 60 to 90 minutes on long trips, especially flights over 4 hours or drives over 6 hours. Calf pumps and ankle circles count.Stay hydrated. Dehydration thickens the blood; aim for water every hour on long travel.Know your inherited risk. If a first-degree relative had a clot before age 50, ask your primary-care provider about Factor V Leiden, prothrombin gene mutation, and antiphospholipid antibody testing.If you are on estrogen-containing birth control or hormone therapy, the baseline clot risk is roughly 2 to 4 times higher. Discuss alternatives with your prescriber if you have other risk factors.Follow-up after a confirmed clot: hematology or vascular medicine for duration-of-therapy decisions (3 months, 6 months, or indefinite based on cause).Why Choose ER of White Rock for Blood Clot Treatment?For families in the White Rock and East Dallas area, what makes our blood-clot workup different from a hospital emergency department:On-site duplex ultrasound for DVT confirmation during your visit, not next-day at an imaging centerOn-site CT pulmonary angiogram for suspected PE with results read by an ER physicianD-dimer with rapid turnaround (10 to 20 minutes) to rule in or rule out as part of the Wells workupBoard-certified emergency physicians 24/7, not on-call from another buildingAnticoagulation started in the ER with a clear bridge to outpatient follow-upDirect hospital transfer coordinated with the receiving cardiology or pulmonology team if admission is neededThe 2023 ED Benchmarking Alliance national median for a hospital-attached emergency department in the Dallas area is 142 minutes from door to provider. Our median is under 10 minutes. For a possible PE, that gap is the difference between intervention and a worse outcome. Get Blood Clot Treatment When is leg pain a blood-clot emergency vs something else?The 30-second answer: if the leg pain is one-sided, with swelling and warmth, come to the ER. If both legs hurt evenly after a workout, urgent care or primary care is fine. Pulmonary embolism is the third most common cardiovascular cause of death. It is frequently misread as anxiety or muscle strain.Choose ER of White Rock when:One leg is swollen, warm, or tender and the other is notCalf or thigh pain that worsens when you flex your foot upward (Homans’ sign)Sudden shortness of breath, pleuritic chest pain, or coughing up blood. Call 911 if severe.Fast heart rate that does not slow with restYou have a recent surgery, long flight, cast or boot, cancer treatment, or active pregnancy or postpartum windowUrgent care or primary care is likely fine when:Both legs ache evenly after a workout, hike, or long day on your feetVisible varicose veins with mild discomfort but no swelling on one sideA muscle strain or cramp that resolves with rest, stretching, and hydrationA bruise with localized tenderness and visible discolorationAlways come in if you are unsure. A DVT or PE missed at home is a far worse outcome than a muscle strain seen in the ER. The CDC reports up to half of people with DVT have no symptoms at all. About a third of untreated proximal DVTs progress to PE. We can rule it in or out with duplex ultrasound, d-dimer, and CT within 90 minutes of your arrival.Emergency Care for Blood Clots Near YouIf you or a loved one needs emergency care for blood clots in Dallas, Texas, visit ER of White Rock for immediate medical attention. Early detection and treatment can prevent life-threatening complications. Contact Us Now Visit Us TodayIf you are in the White Rock, Lake Highlands, Lakewood, or East Dallas area and you suspect a blood clot, ER of White Rock evaluates and treats on site. text: About ER of White RockAt ER of White Rock, we are your trusted partner in emergency medical care, dedicated to serving the Dallas, TX, community with compassion, expertise, and minimal wait times. Our mission is simple: to deliver high-quality emergency treatment when you need it most. We are open and ready to help you 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.Our Commitment to ExcellenceWhen a medical crisis strikes, time is your most valuable asset. Our facility is staffed by a dedicated team of experienced doctors and nurses who are fully prepared to treat severe health issues, from heart attacks to strokes (see the CDC’s heart attack warning signs). We provide immediate medical intervention for everything from painful fractures to complex, life-threatening traumas.Fast Medical Attention: Get evaluated and treated by a physician right away.Complete Patient Care: Expert solutions for both children and adults.Minimal Wait Times: We prioritize your health so you never have to sit in a crowded lobby.State-of-the-Art Equipment: We utilize on-site digital imaging and lab diagnostics.Compassionate Staff: Experience a calm, private, and supportive healing environment.Always Open: Our emergency room is ready to serve you every hour of the year.By pairing modern diagnostic tools with a medical team that truly cares about your recovery, we deliver precise answers and fast relief. You receive premium emergency treatment exactly when you need it. Call Now For Emergency Care A Culture of Compassion We understand that emergencies are stressful. From the moment you walk through our doors, our team prioritizes not only your physical health but also your emotional well-being. Everyone is treated with personalized attention. Accreditation & Safety ER of White Rock meets the highest standards of emergency care. Our facility adheres to strict safety protocols, and our team undergoes continuous training to stay ahead of medical advancements. Your health and safety are our top priorities. Join Our Mission We’re honored to be Dallas’s go-to emergency clinic, and we strive every day to earn your trust. Whether you’re a longtime resident or new to the area, we’re here for you, ready to care deeply and restore health with excellence.Why Choose ER of White Rock?When a health crisis happens, you need immediate answers. Our Dallas emergency center is designed from the ground up to get you fast, effective medical attention when it matters most. We prioritize your health by ensuring you are evaluated by a physician with minimal wait times, day or night.Always Open: Medical emergencies do not stick to business hours. We are fully staffed and ready to treat you 24 hours a day, every day of the year.Expert Medical Staff: Your health is in the hands of seasoned doctors and registered nurses who specialize in severe trauma and critical illness.Advanced Diagnostics: We utilize modern on-site imaging and laboratory testing to figure out exactly what is wrong in minutes instead of hours.Dedicated to Dallas: We are a proud neighborhood facility committed to keeping local families, individuals, and visitors safe and healthy. OUR PEOPLEOur Emergency Care TeamEmergency care at ER of White Rock is delivered by Texas-licensed registered nurses, on site 24 hours a day.
